comment: Cards the daily snapshot job prices (POCKETFOLIO-PRICING.md §3). The app is backendless, so CI cannot know what users hold — add the cards you own here (Settings lists the ones missing and copies these rows for you). `id` is the pokemontcg.io card id the app stores on holdings. `setTotal` is the printed set size (the 102 in 4/102): a row from a set of another size is rejected, because a card number alone matched Base Set 2 for a Base Set Charizard. `setMatch` is a fragment the matched row's set name must contain — promos carry no `x/y` numbering, so it is the only guard against binding to a same-named card from another set. `pptSetId` pins PPT's own set id when a name search keeps landing on the wrong printing. `image` pins a picture when the provider has no usable scan — the Japanese catalog is missing many, and a reprint that shares the artwork beats an empty box; it never changes what is priced. `pcQuery` overrides the auto-built PriceCharting search. A JAPANESE print gets its own entry: the English id with an `@jp` suffix plus `language: "japanese"` — the app reads the @jp snapshot entry for holdings flagged as Japanese slabs. GRADED prices come from eBay's own sold listings (scripts/scrape-ebay-sold.mjs, TASK-ebay-direct.md): `grades` lists the grades held, `cert` is the PSA certificate, and `psaTitle` is the PSA label title copied VERBATIM from the cert page on psacard.com — it is the eBay search string, because sellers copy it from the slab, and it carries the edition (1ST EDITION) with it. A graded card with no `psaTitle` is not searched and gets no graded price: never make one up from the card name.

cards.name: Togepi
cards.setName: Gold Silver to a New World
cards.note: The physical card is the CoroCoro Comic June 1999 promo, catalogued by TCGplayer as product 617258 (CoroCoro Promotional Cards) — that is where the picture comes from. But eBay sellers and PSA both title it 'Gold, Silver, to a New World...', so the graded sales land on product 575874 and that set is where the prices are. 617258 has zero graded sales. Priced there, pictured here, on purpose.
cards.pcQuery: togepi corocoro comics japanese promo pokemon
cards.psaTitle: 1999 POKEMON JAPANESE GOLD, SILVER, TO A NEW WORLD... TOGEPI

cards.name: Ancient Mew
cards.note: The Power of One movie promo (2000), PSA-slabbed as "2000 Pokemon Game Movie". TCGplayer keeps two Ancient Mews in the same set — 108589 (this one, English) and 482427 "Ancient Mew (Japanese Exclusive Print)" — so setMatch alone cannot tell them apart and nameExact pins the English one. Graded copies are by definition out of the sealed sleeve; sealed prices are a different market and are not what this row tracks.

cards.name: Charmander
cards.note: The Obsidian Flames Elite Trainer Box promo, TCGplayer 512035, confirmed by the owner. PPT set 22872 is "SV: Scarlet & Violet Promo Cards" and holds BOTH 512035 and 512036, "Charmander - 044 (Pokemon Center Exclusive)" — same set, same number 044, the stamped one worth more. nameExact cannot separate them because PPT's name string varies by set, so the variant is excluded by name. The setId is pinned because searching by name cannot reach this card: a probe of 80 Charmander rows found it 33rd, so neither the default page of 3 nor a widened 20 ever saw it. If the physical card carries a Pokemon Center stamp, this row is the wrong one.
cards.pcQuery: charmander svp 044 scarlet violet promo pokemon
